mainTopic: Whether a mistaken בתולה keeps a מנה, the groom who was alone with his bride in יהודה, and the כתובות of כהנים' daughters.
overview: The amud opens with רבה, who learns from a ברייתא that a woman married as a בתולה who turns out to be a בעולה still gets a כתובה of a מנה. רב אשי rejects this. Normally she gets nothing; the ברייתא is special because she had been married before. A second version puts the same exchange on our משנה about a בתולה מן הנישואין. The גמרא then explains how far each version reaches. A new משנה rules that a groom in יהודה who ate at his father-in-law's house without witnesses cannot make a טענת בתולים. The גמרא learns from this that customs differed within יהודה, and brings a ברייתא of רבי יהודה listing customs of יהודה and the גליל. אביי, רבא and רב אשי each explain which custom the ברייתא's closing rule refers to. Finally, a new משנה gives every widow a מנה and says a court of כהנים collected 400 זוז for a virgin. רב אשי begins to explain a ברייתא that gives a כהן's widow 200, through two ordinances, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה learns that a mistaken בתולה still gets 100
steps.stepSummary: רבה infers from the ברייתא that a woman married as a בתולה who is found to be a בעולה still gets a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This teaches us that if a man married a woman thinking she was a בתולה, and she turned out to be a בעולה, she still gets a כתובה of 100.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה draws a general rule out of the ברייתא the גמרא just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the woman was assumed to be a בתולה but was found not to be, and she still got a מנה. רבה reads this as a general rule: discovering she is a בעולה does not cancel her כתובה completely. It only lowers it from 200 to 100.

keyTerms.meaning: "This teaches us": a rule drawn out of an earlier source
On the assumption that she is a virgin
A woman who is not a virgin

phrases.english: Rabba said: This teaches us,
if he married her on the assumption she was a virgin,
and she was found to be a non-virgin,
she has a marriage contract of one hundred.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman married as a בתולה who is found to be a בעולה gets a כתובה of a מנה.

steps.title: רב אשי: normally she gets nothing; here she was married before
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects רבה's inference. Normally such a woman gets no כתובה at all, but here the first husband had already married her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In general, I'll tell you, she gets nothing at all. This case is different, because a first husband had already married her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רבה. He says the ברייתא is a special case and cannot teach a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a normal case, a woman married as a בתולה who turns out to be a בעולה loses her whole כתובה, because the marriage rested on a mistake. Here the second husband knew she had been married before, so he should have expected she might not be a בתולה. That is why she still keeps a מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In general, in an ordinary case
"Really, I'll tell you": introduces the speaker's own position

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
In general, really, I will tell you
she has nothing at all,
phrases.notes: He means no כתובה at all.

phrases.english: but here it is different,
because the first husband had married her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּעָלְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ לֵית לַהּ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's general inference by limiting the ברייתא to its special facts.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the generalization, not the ruling of the ברייתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's woman had been married before, so the second husband should have suspected she was not a בתולה. Nothing can be learned from it about an ordinary case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 100 here comes from a special factor and is not the normal result of a mistaken בתולה.

steps.title: Why not suspect she was unfaithful during אירוסין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we are not worried that she was unfaithful after the second husband betrothed her. If she was, she would be forbidden to him and get no כתובה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let's worry that maybe she was unfaithful while she was already his (betrothed)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the case of the ברייתא. Since we know she was not with her first husband, how did she lose her בתולים? Maybe it happened during her אירוסין to the second husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she lost her בתולים with another man after the second husband's קידושין, that is unfaithfulness. She would then be forbidden to him and lose her כתובה entirely. So why does the ברייתא give her a מנה?

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, "under him": while she was bound to him

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps she was unfaithful while under him!
phrases.notes: "Under him" means after the second husband had made קידושין with her.

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the ברייתא that she gets a מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her missing בתולים might come from unfaithfulness during אירוסין, which would leave her with no כתובה at all.

steps.title: רב שרביא: he married her right after the קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא explains that the case is one where he made קידושין and lived with her immediately, so there was no time to be unfaithful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said: The case is where he betrothed her and was with her right away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the marriage came immediately after the קידושין, there was no window of time in which she was betrothed to him and could have been with someone else. So her missing בתולים must come from before the קידושין, and the worry is gone.

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said:
For example, where he betrothed her and had relations with her immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ וּבָעַל לְאַלְתַּר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was time between קידושין and marriage, so she might have been unfaithful.
steps.terutzMaskana: There was no gap at all, so unfaithfulness during אירוסין is impossible.
steps.whatToRemember: First version: רבה learns from the ברייתא that she gets a מנה. רב אשי says normally she gets nothing, and the ברייתא is special because she was married before. רב שרביא removes the worry about unfaithfulness: he married her right after the קידושין.

steps.title: Second version: the same discussion placed on our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second version that attaches רבה's statement to the משנה about a בתולה who became a widow, divorcée or חלוצה מן הנישואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this on our משנה: A בתולה who is a widow, divorcée, or חלוצה from marriage gets a כתובה of 100, and there is no claim about her בתולים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second version of the whole discussion, this time on the משנה. It first quotes the line of the משנה that the discussion will build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says these women get only a מנה and their husband cannot make a טענת בתולים. Even if she is physically a בתולה, having been married lowers her כתובה. This line is the base for the question and for רבה's inference that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a second version)
A woman released from יבום through חליצה
After full marriage (as opposed to after אירוסין only)
A husband's claim that his wife was not a virgin

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on our mishna:
A virgin who is a widow, a divorcée,
or a ḥalutza, from marriage,
their marriage contract is one hundred,
and they are not subject to a claim about virginity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the same discussion, based on a different source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בתולה widow, divorcée or חלוצה מן הנישואין gets a מנה and is not subject to a טענת בתולים.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same רבה and רב אשי exchange, attached to a different source.

steps.title: How can a married woman still be a בתולה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a woman can be a בתולה after full marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בתולה from marriage: how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the משנה's case is even possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נישואין usually means the couple lived together, so it seems strange to call her a בתולה. The גמרא wants to know what situation the משנה has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: A virgin from marriage —
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתוּלָה מִן הַנִּישּׂוּאִין הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case fits a woman who is a בתולה after full נישואין

steps.title: She entered the חופה but they never lived together
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where she entered the חופה but the marriage was never consummated.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, she entered the חופה and was not with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by describing the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חופה makes her fully married (נשואה) even if nothing physical happened. Once she is widowed or divorced, she is a בתולה מן הנישואין.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding canopy, which creates full marriage

phrases.english: For example, where she entered the wedding canopy
and did not have relations.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She entered the חופה and was never with her husband.

steps.title: רבה learns the 100 rule from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה infers from this משנה that a woman married as a בתולה who is found to be a בעולה gets a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This teaches us that if a man married a woman thinking she was a בתולה, and she turned out to be a בעולה, her כתובה is 100.
steps.whatsHappening: In this second version, רבה draws the same general rule, now from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says her husband has no טענת בתולים and she gets a מנה. רבה understands this to include a case where she turns out not to be a בתולה: she still keeps her מנה. He generalizes this to every woman married as a בתולה who is found to be a בעולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her כתובה, the marriage contract payment

phrases.english: Rabba said: This teaches us,
if he married her on the assumption she was a virgin
and she was found to be a non-virgin,
her marriage contract is one hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת, כְּנָסָהּ בְּחֶזְקַת בְּתוּלָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman married as a בתולה who is found to be a בעולה gets a מנה.

steps.title: רב אשי: here it is different because she entered a חופה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי again rejects רבה. Normally such a woman gets nothing, but here she had already entered a חופה with a first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, I'll tell you, in general she gets nothing at all. Here it is different, because she had entered a חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the same kind of rejection as in the first version, now fitted to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who already entered a חופה should be suspected of no longer being a בתולה, so the second husband took that risk on himself. That is why she keeps a מנה. In an ordinary case of a mistaken בתולה, she would lose the whole כתובה.
steps.whatToRemember: In this version too, רב אשי says a woman married as a בתולה who turns out to be a בעולה normally gets nothing. She keeps a מנה here only because her earlier חופה should have warned the husband. Step 12 shows how far each version reaches.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Really, I will tell you, in general
she has nothing at all,
but here it is different,
because she entered the wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ בְּעָלְמָא לֵית לַהּ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's generalization from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the general rule, not the ruling of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Having entered a חופה before is a special factor that should have warned the husband, so no general rule can be learned from this case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this version, רבה's inference from the משנה is rejected: רב אשי explains the מנה through the woman's earlier חופה. Step 12 shows that this version still leaves רבה's proof from the ברייתא in place.

steps.title: Why not worry she was unfaithful to the second husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's explanation: maybe she committed adultery after the second husband betrothed her, which would make her lose her כתובה completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe she was unfaithful while she was already betrothed to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling that she gets a מנה. It asks why we don't suspect the woman was unfaithful after the second husband betrothed her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבה and רב אשי agree she gets a מנה here. But the missing בתולים might have another cause: she could have been unfaithful between the second husband's קידושין and the wedding. If so, she would be forbidden to him and get no כתובה at all, not even a מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: While under him, meaning while betrothed to him

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps she was unfaithful while under him!
phrases.notes: 'Under him' means after the second husband betrothed her but before the wedding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's reading in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that this woman receives a מנה at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her lost בתולים might come from adultery during her betrothal to the second husband. That would make her lose everything.

steps.title: He betrothed her and married her right away
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא explains that the case is one where the second husband betrothed her and had relations with her immediately, so there was no time for her to be unfaithful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said: The case is where he betrothed her and lived with her immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא answers the challenge. In this case there was no gap between the betrothal and the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry only works if there was a stretch of time between קידושין and the marriage. רב שרביא sets the case where there was no such time, so the suspicion has no room. רב אשי's explanation stands.

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said:
For example, where he betrothed her and had relations with her immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ וּבָעַל לְאַלְתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was time between the betrothal and the marriage for her to be unfaithful
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one with no gap, so there was no chance for adultery during the betrothal

steps.title: Comparing the two versions of the exchange
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the two versions relate. Whoever places the exchange on the ברייתא would surely apply it to the משנה. Whoever places it on the משנה would not apply it to the ברייתא, because there the husband can say he relied on the witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever teaches this exchange on the ברייתא would say it all the more so on the משנה. But whoever teaches it on the משנה would not say it on the ברייתא, because the husband can tell her: I relied on the witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and compares the two versions of רבה and רב אשי's argument. It shows that the two versions lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא there were witnesses that she was never alone with the first husband. If רב אשי rejects רבה even there, he surely rejects him in the משנה, where there are no such witnesses. But if the exchange was only said on the משנה, רבה's proof from the ברייתא still holds, since the husband can say he married her trusting the witnesses that she was a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches it (this exchange) on
A teaching of the תנאים left out of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The version on the ברייתא is broader and covers the משנה too. The version on the משנה is narrower and leaves רבה's proof from the ברייתא in place, because of the husband's claim 'I relied on witnesses'.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the ברייתא —
all the more so on the משנה,
and the one who teaches it on the משנה —
but not on the ברייתא,
because he can say to her:
I relied on the witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַבָּרַיְיתָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַמַּתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רבה and רב אשי discussion by comparing its two versions
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under the ברייתא version, רב אשי's rejection applies to both sources. Under the משנה version, רבה's inference from the ברייתא survives.

steps.title: A groom who eats at his father-in-law's house in יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: in יהודה, a groom who ate at his father-in-law's house during the betrothal with no witnesses present cannot later claim his bride was not a בתולה, since we assume he was alone with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who eats at his father-in-law's house in יהודה without witnesses cannot make a claim about בתולים, because he is alone with her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It says a groom in יהודה who spent time at his bride's family home without witnesses loses his right to a בתולים complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The custom in יהודה let the groom be alone with his betrothed. If no witnesses can show otherwise, we suspect he himself was with her. So he cannot blame her for not being a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim that the bride was not a virgin

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who eats at his father-in-law's house in Judea
without witnesses —
cannot make a claim about virginity,
because he is alone with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A groom in יהודה who ate at his father-in-law's house without witnesses loses his טענת בתולים, since we assume he was alone with her.

steps.title: Learning from the word 'one who eats'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the משנה says 'one who eats', which suggests that in some places in יהודה the groom did not eat at his father-in-law's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה says 'one who eats', this implies that even in יהודה there was a place where he did not eat there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the משנה's wording. This sets up אביי's conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every groom in יהודה ate at his father-in-law's house, the משנה could just say 'in יהודה, he cannot claim'. The phrase 'one who eats' hints that this was not done everywhere in יהודה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Since it teaches 'one who eats',
by implication there is a place
in Judea too where he does not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the משנה in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'one who eats' implies that not every place in יהודה had this custom.

steps.title: אביי: customs varied within יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes from the wording that even within יהודה, different places had different customs.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that even in יהודה, customs differed from place to place.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי states the conclusion from the inference in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought יהודה had one custom across the whole region. אביי says the משנה's wording shows the custom differed from town to town even there.

keyTerms.meaning: There are different places (with different customs)

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this
that in Judea too there are different places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 14's inference
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even within יהודה, customs about the groom and his betrothed differed by place.

steps.title: רבי יהודה describes the old custom in יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: in יהודה, originally the groom and bride were left alone together for a short time before the חופה, so he would feel at ease with her. In the גליל they did not do this.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא, רבי יהודה said: In יהודה, at first they would leave the groom and bride alone for a short while before they entered the חופה, so he would feel comfortable with her. In the גליל they did not do this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up אביי. It shows that the custom of leaving the couple alone depended on the place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה describes a real custom of letting the couple be alone before the חופה, and says the גליל did not follow it. This shows that customs about this changed from place to place, which supports אביי's point. It also explains the משנה's worry that the groom may have been alone with his bride.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
They would leave them alone together
He would feel at ease with her
The northern region of ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: The rule in the משנה depends on local custom. Where couples were left alone before the חופה, the groom cannot later complain about בתולים without witnesses.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In Judea, at first

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ מְיַיחֲדִין אֶת הֶחָתָן וְאֶת הַכַּלָּה
phrases.english: they would leave the groom and the bride alone together
for a short time before they entered the wedding canopy,
so that he would feel at ease with her,
and in the Galilee they did not do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's conclusion in step 15
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that customs about leaving the couple alone differed by place
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה describing the custom in יהודה and its absence in the גליל

steps.title: Two groomsmen checked the couple at the wedding
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: in early times in יהודה, two שושבינין were appointed, one for the groom and one for the bride, to check them as they entered the חופה. The גליל did not do this.
steps.simpleTranslation: In יהודה, in early times, they would appoint two groomsmen for the couple, one for him and one for her, to check the groom and the bride when they entered the חופה. In the גליל they did not do this.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה continues with a second custom from יהודה. Two שושבינין were appointed to check the couple at the start of their married life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the checking was that neither side could cheat about the signs of בתולים. Checking like this only makes sense if the couple had not already been alone together before the חופה. So this seems to be a different practice from the first custom in step 16. That fits אביי's point that places within יהודה had different customs.

keyTerms.meaning: Groomsmen or attendants of the bride and groom
Their entry into the wedding canopy
The Galilee, the northern region of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: In Judea, at first,
they would appoint for them two groomsmen,
one for him and one for her,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְמַשְׁמֵשׁ אֶת הֶחָתָן וְאֶת הַכַּלָּה
phrases.english: in order to examine the groom and the bride
at the time of their entry into the wedding canopy,
and in the Galilee they would not do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיהוּדָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַעֲמִידִין לָהֶם שְׁנֵי שׁוֹשְׁבִינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of רבי יהודה cited in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that customs differed within יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of the ברייתא of רבי יהודה

steps.title: The groomsmen slept in the couple's house
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds: in early times in יהודה, the שושבינין slept in the same house as the bride and groom. The גליל did not do this.
steps.simpleTranslation: In יהודה, in early times, the groomsmen would sleep in the house where the groom and bride slept. In the גליל they did not do this.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists a third custom from יהודה. The שושבינין stayed overnight in the house where the couple slept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Staying close by let the שושבינין check right after the marriage was completed. This way the groom could not hide the signs of בתולים and then falsely claim she was not a בתולה. The ברייתא again contrasts this with the גליל.

phrases.english: In Judea, at first,
the groomsmen would sleep in the house
in which the groom and bride sleep,
and in the Galilee they would not do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיהוּדָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ שׁוֹשְׁבִינִין יְשֵׁנִים בַּבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another custom to the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Different customs in יהודה versus the גליל

steps.title: Whoever did not follow this custom cannot claim she was not a virgin
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes with a rule: anyone who did not follow 'this custom' cannot make a טענת בתולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who did not act according to this custom cannot make a claim about virginity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a practical rule tied to one of the customs it listed. The wording is vague, and this sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say which custom 'this custom' means. It also says 'whoever did not follow', which makes it sound like the husband loses his claim because he skipped the custom. That vagueness is what the גמרא is about to examine.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim that the bride was not a virgin

phrases.english: And anyone who did not conduct himself in accordance with this custom
cannot make a claim concerning virginity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing rule of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who did not follow 'this custom' loses the right to make a טענת בתולים.

steps.title: Which custom does the rule refer to? Not the first one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which custom the closing rule refers to. If it refers to the first custom, where the couple was left alone before the חופה, the ברייתא should have said 'whoever did follow it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which case does this refer to? If you say it is the first clause, it should have said 'anyone who did follow the custom'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which custom the rule is attached to. It tests the first option and shows that the wording does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first custom, the couple was alone before the חופה. The person who loses his claim is the one who did follow that custom, because maybe he was with her before the wedding. So the words 'did not follow' do not fit that custom.

keyTerms.meaning: To which one? Which case is this about?

phrases.english: Concerning which case?
If we say it refers to the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the custom from step 16, where the couple was left alone before the חופה.

phrases.english: it should have said: 'Anyone who did conduct himself so'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא's closing rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the rule as referring to the first custom (being alone before the חופה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With that custom, it is the man who followed it who loses his claim, so the wording 'did not follow' is the wrong way around.

steps.title: Not the groomsmen custom either
steps.stepSummary: If the rule refers to the later custom of the שושבינין checking the couple, the ברייתא should have said 'whoever was not checked'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it refers to the last clause, it should have said 'anyone who was not checked'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, the שושבינין custom, and shows that this wording does not fit either. Steps 22–25 give the answers of אביי, רבא and רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking by the שושבינין is something done to the couple. The ברייתא would then say 'not checked', not 'did not follow', which sounds like it depends on what the husband himself did. So neither option matches the ברייתא's words.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'whoever did not follow this custom' does not fit the first custom, because there the one who followed it loses his claim. It also does not fit the שושבינין custom, because then it should say 'whoever was not checked'.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the latter clause,
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the custom of the two שושבינין checking the couple.

phrases.english: it should have said: 'Anyone who was not examined'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible reading after the first one was rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the rule as referring to the שושבינין custom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being checked is done to the couple, so the wording should be 'not checked' and not 'did not follow', which points to the husband's own action.

steps.title: אביי: the rule is about the first custom, so read it as 'whoever did follow it'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the question from Step 20. The closing rule really does refer to the first custom, the couple being alone before the חופה. He fixes the wording to 'anyone who DID follow it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It really refers to the first part, and you should read it as 'anyone who followed (the custom).'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question of which custom the closing rule means. He picks the first custom and changes one word of the ברייתא so it makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 showed that if the rule means the first custom, the wording 'did not follow' sounds backwards. A man who WAS alone with his bride is the one who cannot later claim she was not a בתולה. So אביי simply changes the text to 'anyone who did follow it.'

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (I keep my original reading)
The first part of a teaching
Followed a custom, acted in a certain way

phrases.english: Abaye said: Really, it is about the first part,
phrases.notes: The first part means the first custom: the couple was left alone before the חופה.

phrases.english: and read it as: 'Anyone who followed (it).'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 20 and 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to say that a man who did NOT follow the first custom loses his claim, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the rule as 'anyone who DID follow it' cannot make a טענת בתולים.

steps.title: רבא objects: the text clearly says 'did not follow'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's change. The ברייתא openly says 'did not follow,' so we cannot just flip it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But it clearly teaches 'anyone who did NOT follow'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי. You can't just turn 'did not' into 'did' when the text plainly says 'did not.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer works only by reversing the exact wording of the ברייתא. רבא feels that is too big a change. He holds that we should find an explanation that fits the words as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it the case that

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But it teaches 'Anyone who did not follow'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer from Step 22
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It reverses the clear words of the ברייתא instead of explaining them.

steps.title: רבא: someone in the גליל who followed the custom of יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the rule without changing a word. It is about a man living in the גליל who did not follow the local custom but followed יהודה's custom of being alone with the bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what it means: Anyone who did not follow the custom of the גליל while in the גליל, but followed the custom of יהודה in the גליל, cannot make a טענת בתולים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer. 'Did not follow this custom' means did not follow the גליל's custom, and instead was alone with his bride the way people did in יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'did not follow' stay as they are. They just point to the custom of the גליל, where the couple was not left alone. A man who broke that custom and was alone with the bride, as in יהודה, loses his טענת בתולים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier answer and giving a new one)
A husband's claim that his bride was not a בתולה

steps.whatToRemember: רבא keeps the ברייתא's words. 'Did not follow' means did not follow the גליל's custom of keeping the couple apart.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said, this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁלֹּא נָהַג מִנְהַג גָּלִיל בַּגָּלִיל,
phrases.english: Anyone who did not follow the custom of the Galilee in the Galilee,
but instead followed the custom of Judea in the Galilee —
cannot make a claim about virginity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after rejecting אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining which custom 'this custom' means, with no change to the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'This custom' seemed to mean יהודה's custom, so 'did not follow' sounded backwards.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'This custom' is the גליל's custom. A man in the גליל who acted like the people of יהודה cannot claim.

steps.title: רב אשי: the rule is about the later custom, read as 'whoever was not checked'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the rule refers to the last custom, the שושבינין checking the couple. He reads it as 'anyone who was not checked.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It really refers to the last part, and read it as 'anyone who was not checked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. He picks the second option from Step 21, the checking by the שושבינין, and reads the rule in that light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 asked: if the rule means the checking custom, it should have said 'whoever was not checked.' רב אשי accepts that and says that is indeed the meaning. A man who was not checked by the שושבינין cannot make a טענת בתולים.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Really, it is about the last part,
phrases.notes: The last part means the custom of the שושבינין checking the bride and groom.

phrases.english: and read it as: 'Anyone who was not checked.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of Steps 20 and 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the rule as being about the later custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the rule meant the checking custom, 'did not follow' seemed like the wrong wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'anyone who was not checked' cannot make a טענת בתולים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three explanations of the closing line: אביי (the first custom, changed to 'did follow'), רבא (the גליל's custom, no change), and רב אשי (the checking custom, 'was not checked').

steps.title: New משנה: every widow gets a מנה, and the כהנים collected 400 for a virgin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that both a regular widow and a widow from a כהן family get a כתובה of a מנה. It also reports that a court of כהנים collected 400 זוז for a virgin, and the חכמים did not stop them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both a widow from a regular Jewish family and a widow from a כהן family have a כתובה of a מנה. A court of כהנים used to collect 400 זוז for a virgin, and the חכמים did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the amount of a widow's כתובה and tells us about a special higher amount the כהנים used for virgins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנה is 100 זוז, the standard widow's כתובה. The משנה says a כהן family's widow gets no extra. For a virgin from a כהן family, though, the כהנים' court doubled the usual 200 to 400, and the חכמים allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (a new one starts here)
The marriage contract, with the money owed to the wife
A court made up of כהנים
Did not protest or stop them

phrases.english: MISHNA: Both a widow who is an Israelite woman
and a widow from a family of priests —
her marriage contract is one hundred (zuz).
A court of priests

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ גּוֹבִין לִבְתוּלָה אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז,
phrases.english: would collect four hundred zuz for a virgin,
and the Sages did not protest against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת אַלְמְנַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַחַת אַלְמְנַת כֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every widow, including from a כהן family, gets a כתובה of a מנה. The כהנים' court collected 400 זוז for a virgin, with the חכמים' consent.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a כהן's widow gets 200
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying the widow from a כהן family has a כתובה of 200. This sets up a contradiction with the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: A widow from a כהן family has a כתובה of 200.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different amount. This is setting up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said a כהן's widow gets a מנה (100). This ברייתא says 200, double that. The clash is the next move.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא on the new משנה begins

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
And a widow from a family of priests — her marriage contract is two hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source on the same topic as the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא, a כהן's widow has a כתובה of 200.

steps.title: But the משנה says a כהן's widow gets only a מנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא contradicts the משנה, which put both widows at a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: Both a regular widow and a widow from a כהן family have a כתובה of a מנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by quoting the משנה, which gives a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 100 for a כהן's widow, and the ברייתא says 200. Both cannot be right as they stand, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת אַלְמְנַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַחַת אַלְמְנַת כֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: Both an Israelite widow and a widow from a family of priests
their marriage contract is one hundred!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ברייתא of Step 27 against the משנה of Step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's amount of 200 for a כהן's widow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה clearly gives a מנה (100) for a כהן's widow, which contradicts 200.

steps.title: רב אשי: there were two ordinances, and the first was 400 for a virgin and a מנה for a widow
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי begins to answer. The כהנים made two ordinances at different times, and the first one gave 400 to a virgin and a מנה to a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There were two ordinances. At first they set 400 זוז for a virgin and a מנה for a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts his answer by saying the rules changed over time. Here he describes only the first ordinance, which matches the משנה. The second ordinance comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and the ברייתא are not really fighting. They describe two different periods. The first ordinance (400 for a virgin, 100 for a widow) is what the משנה records, which prepares us to hear the second ordinance behind the ברייתא's 200.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinance, a rule enacted by a court

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב אשי is rejecting the משנה. He says both sources are correct, each for a different time.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁתֵּי תַּקָּנוֹת הֲווֹ,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: There were two ordinances,

phrases.aramaic: מֵעִיקָּרָא תַּקִּינוּ לִבְתוּלָה אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז,
phrases.english: at first they enacted for a virgin four hundred zuz,
phrases.notes: 'They' is the court of כהנים from the משנה.

phrases.english: and for a widow one hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁתֵּי תַּקָּנוֹת הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the contradiction from Step 28
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to give clashing amounts for the same widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ordinance gave 400 to a virgin and a מנה to a widow, matching the משנה. The second ordinance is still to come.
